as_told.title: Five people at the legacy company: engineers, no physicists

plain: Sometime in the 2010s, a senior vice president at an old, established aerospace company, a materials scientist, said his company's work on recovered crashed craft had never had a single physicist on it. Eric W. Davis, a scientist who has worked for the Pentagon, tells Michels he asked the man where his physicists were and was told: "we don't have any. We never did," because the company was only allowed to keep about a handful of people on the work. Davis also says from his own contact that he knew of five such people at that company, met two of them, and saw one routinely through a Pentagon study he calls OSAP; one, a woman, was a mathematician working as chief of security. If true, it would mean the craft were handled by a tiny team with no one trained to understand how they work.
